content:
Moving the following message from Sergei:

Hi Markus,

At some point, when you have time, do you want to take a look at the lack of (\forall n. x =n= y) \implies x = y axiom in some of your examples? I wonder if quotients can fix it.
During the Iris workshop, I've had a small discussion with Robbert, and he confirmed that the intention for OFE/COFE was that they satisfy separation, and the reason Equiv was introduced was precisely the lack of usable quotients in Rocq, and that Rocq by default doesn't assume any axioms.
If it's something that can be enforced with quotients, I can take a look on how to refactor the codebase to use equality, and we won't need to maintain grw.
I think the general idea is that for all OFEs X that don't satisfy (\forall n. x =n= y) \implies x = y by default, X/Equiv should satisfy it.

While not changing expressiveness of Lean Iris, it can a) prevent proof size inflation that we currently have; b) spare us of introducing a fragile tactic (even if grw is maintained not by us, setoid rewrite is unstable even in Rocq, e.g., f : X -n> Y -n> Z, y1 y2 : Y, y1 \equiv y2, f x y1 \equiv f x y2 was not working by setoid rewrite 1.5 yrs ago by default).

There also might be a benefit for your projects, since with separation you can actually show that OFEs are ultrametric spaces, as in Mathlib, and reuse more stuff related to probabilities.

My reply:

Nice! I agree with your analysis: I think that if we can find evidence that quotients do not lose us generality then I think it's clear that the advantages would be worth it. How about this for a plan:

  • I will try to see if quotients can make my math experiments Leibniz. I do suspect that quotients will work for the instance, what I'd want to see is if the math is still nice enough when working through the quotient.
  • Perhaps you could feel out the ergonomics of a quotient OFE? If the old API can be converted to a Leibniz OFE by "QuotientO", that would be strong evidence that the refactor won't lose generality (universe issues & tactic support is my only real concern). This general construction should probably be present in some form anyways!
  • There was also some discussion about quotients in König's thesis and the old README if I recall--I think some of their problems were resolved by the Leibniz UPred change but we should refresh ourselves on their read of the situation.
  • We should also try to dig up examples of Iris logics that make nontrivial use of equivalences. If we could port some of their resources, and then make them Leibniz, that would also be strong evidence that we won't lose generality. There might be none, and that would be awesome.

Now that we're over the halfway point with the logic, an affirmative answer to these questions would give me a lot of confidence that we won't "paint us into a corner" so to speak. In which case, this could really be a major improvement to the framework as a whole.

Opening this up for other comments, but basically, I think we're at a place now where if the Leibniz specialization works, we can be confident that it will work for the future usages of Iris lean. In which case, it's a wonderful idea!

Some work on point 4: I had my agents produce a report on the usage of non-leibniz OFE's from the projects on the Iris webpage. Here is the report, beware that it is AI text: non_leibniz_ofe_report.md. From what I see, the custom ones are mostly just lifting equivalence across functions, subtyping by validity, or quotienting by a simple formula. I think we have tricks for expressing all of these as Leibniz relations in Lean... I'm much more convinced now that getting rid of OFE equivalence won't stop us form porting logics in the future.

Some ones I don't understand as much:

  • vPred from iGPS. I don't really understand the construction so I find it hard to evaluate.
  • The resources from GITrees defined as a fixpoint. I don't super understand Sergei's change to the COFE solver, maybe he can weigh in if such a thing is Leibniz?

I will also say I've convinced myself that point 1 is not a problem either. I think it's clear to me that even if there are some headaches converting representations (eg. up to sets of measure 0 or something) they will be able to be worked around.

Thanks for looking into it!
I'll take a look at vpred today.

From gitree side, gitrees are Leibniz under very mild assumptions (cf. Fix.lean example) that in practice always hold. Basically, a) base cofes are Leibniz, which holds, since they are usually discrete; b) effects use Leibniz preserving functors for signatures (so far, all used effects did that)
Moreover, if we move from OFEs in setoids to OFEs in types, all functors will be Leibniz preserving, so it's going to be a non-issue.
If it's this one, then it looks like function space with two Leibniz components.

I think another way to look at it is (what I assume) Ralf (@ralfj ) meant in the Iris chat. In the MoDuRes times setoids and OFEs were separate typeclasses, and Leibniz is a property related to OFEs to have funext/propext-like properties and quotients-like constructions. In the presence of funext/propext and quotients (or choice, if there're no quotients) it should be possible to do the same constructions using usual equalities. I'll look for references, but I'm pretty sure that setoid type theory can be syntactically translated to intensional type theory with funext/propext and quotients.

I guess my point here is that in fully constructive setting it makes total sense to do setoids for Iris, but Lean has axioms and quotients by default (i.e., we don't move to more restricted models, since we don't assume anything new), so it might save a lot of machinery and effort to use equalities instead of setoids.

Moreover, it seems a lot of constructions in Mathlib don't use setoids, so if we move to equalities we can actually show that OFE/COFE are ultrametrics, and it might be of help in projects that can reuse some parts of it. On top of that, it might be of help with tactics, because it seems some tactics that use rewriting are tuned to use propositional equalities.

I've made a toy POC that implements Leibniz-by-construction OFEs by using quotients, and tests it on Agree.
If we reach consensus on equiv/eq change, then OFE constructions with use quotient-like construction, like Agree, can be implemented in a similar manner with explicit quotients, and manual Equiv-typed terms can be replaced with rw/simp tactics.

I think my biggest concern that I would like to discuss about this change are examples of OFEs that rely on measure theory that are not Leibniz. I don't know enough of the constructions that are used there (and this particular part of Mathlib), so I can't evaluate if the same tricks apply there, so it would be nice to check it, before we commit to this change.

the current iris rocq is not directly derived from the MoDuRes development, its Setoid approach is inherited from robbert's PhD thesis... but those are probably pretty similar since it's the standard in rocq. rocq has pretty good generalized rewriting and defaults to "no axioms" (and has no quotients) so Setoids are the standard thing to do.
IOW, I agree with what you said :)

Sergei Stepanenko said:

I think my biggest concern that I would like to discuss about this change are examples of OFEs that rely on measure theory that are not Leibniz.

This was a worry for me as well, but I don't think it should be a blocker. I have a feeling that everything _I_ want to do with measures and limits can be expressed neatly as a quotient, and while I don't think I'll have time to explore that in the near future, I'm not worried.

We should also try applying your generic quotient construction to PartialMap sometime--I think the right way to make this change for maps is to change all internal references to use ExtensionalPartialMap, and to have a canonical PartialMap to ExtensionalPartialMap construction so that API surface is preserved.

ralfj said:

the current iris rocq is not directly derived from the MoDuRes development, its Setoid approach is inherited from robbert's PhD thesis... but those are probably pretty similar since it's the standard in rocq. rocq has pretty good generalized rewriting and defaults to "no axioms" (and has no quotients) so Setoids are the standard thing to do.

Oh, I didn't know, thanks for clarifying! :)
Btw, could you please send a link to two distance thing that you mentioned? I would like to take a look out of curiosity, if it's public.

Oki, I'll start experimenting with it early next week then. I think I'll probably create PRs in stages to avoid making big changes:

  1. Partial map -> Extensional partial map;
  2. Explicit quotient constructions for implicitly quotiented OFEs (i.e., the ones that don't preserve Leibniz, as agreement before), by the end of it, all OFEs in the project should either be Leibniz or Leibniz preserving;
  3. OFE interface change (that is going to be breaking, so I will go over active PRs at this point to see if everything lands well, and help with adapting);
  4. Proofs simplification by changing manually constructed equiv-typed (at this stage eq-typed) terms (the biggest part) to rw/simp.

I don't have a precise timescale for it, but will try to make some estimates early next week as well.

Sergei Stepanenko said:

Btw, could you please send a link to two distance thing that you mentioned? I would like to take a look out of curiosity, if it's public.

yeah it's all public
the weird metric is defined at https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/lambda-rust/-/blob/master/lambda-rust/typing/type.v?ref_type=heads#L262
and used for the fixpoint in https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/lambda-rust/-/blob/master/lambda-rust/typing/fixpoint.v?ref_type=heads
this is probably incomprehensible though^^
I have a very brief discussion of the high-level point of this in my thesis on page 139

Sergei Stepanenko said:

Oki, I'll start experimenting with it early next week then. I think I'll probably create PRs in stages to avoid making big changes:

Update on the above:
For (2) there's a prepared PR that introduces a Leibniz version of agree, satisfying the same interface.
For (1) there's a draft that depends on (1) and forces lawful maps to be extensional. With that one, all OFEs in the project should be Leibniz/Leibniz-preserving.
For (3) and (4) I think a realistic estimate is a bit more than a week to make a draft PR.
I thought that the cleanest way to do it is to make a PR that changes OFE to use equality, make Equiv an abbrev of Eq with a deprecation note (similar with Equiv-related lemmas), and then start simplifying the existing proofs that use equiv_* lemmas (replacing them with usual rewriting).
At this point, reusing Leibniz instances from (1) and (2) should be enough to show that OFEs in the codebase satisfy the new definition so that there won't be any technical problems.
